questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was my second exchange and I wanted to focus more on it being a good university and having some interesting courses than being able to do a lot of exploring, which was the case for University of Amsterdam. I've been to Amsterdam before and I like the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed my exchange, but during the whole semester we had restrictions due to covid, which made it more difficult to meet up with people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was part at the ESN introduction week, where we got a lot of information and met a lot of people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through De Key, which for me worked out fine. But there is not enough housing for all exchange strudentes, so it is first come first served principle.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I lived more or less in the city center for quite a cheap rent. We were 10 people sharing kitchen, bathrooms and showers and we each had our own room. For a more expensive rent (not necessarily that much more) you can also live with just one roommate or in your own apartment. 
My campus (Science park) is a bit outside the city center (approx 4 km), but it took me 20 min by bike.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found the courses I was interested in on the website and then told my student coordinator at UvA which courses I wanted and she registered me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got the things I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: For me the process was quite easy, just a few emails back and forward.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I would say the level is a lot like UCPH.
One semester consists of 3 blocks, the first 2 are 8 weeks (7 of classes and 1 exam week) and the last is 4 weeks (3 of classes and 1 exam week). Be aware that there are no breaks between the blocks.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say it was a lot like UPCH in the way of teaching, except you have to work more for the ECTS. Plus they have less tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Block 1: 
Condensed Matter 2 : 6 ECTS
Condensed Matter Theory 1 : 3 ECTS
General Relativity : 6 ECTS

Block 2:
Condensed Matter Theory 2 : 3 ECTS
Quantum Optics : 6 ECTS

Block 3:
Condensed Matter Theory 3 : 3 ECTS
Programming c++ : 3 ETCS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Condensed Matter Theory 1+2+3, because we had a very good teacher. But it was a lot of work for 3 ECTS.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I bought the museumcard, which gives access to a lot of museums in The Netherlands. I spent money on going on day trips to other cities in The Netherlands, but I also took a trip to Belgium and Munich. 
I went to cafe and restaurants quite often.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Local transport is quite expensive, so I rented a Swapfiets bike.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ESN have a lot of social events during the semester, both day trips, weekends trips, a social event at uni and so on. Other than that, you can register at Universum (fitness center) or some of the different sport clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed visiting a lot of the museums, so if you are interested in that I can recommend the museumcard (but be aware not all museums/art gallaries are included).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed going on some day trips to see other cities in The Netherlands. I can also recommend meeting up with a friend and go for a walk around the city or go to a cafe (they have lots of them).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say it is very similar to the Danish culture in a lot of ways, so I didn't encounter any clashes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most of the people I spent a lot of time with (that I didn't live with) I met through the ESN introduction week, so I would definitely recommend signing up for that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't know. I would say living in Amsterdam is not that different from living in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Dutch have a very strong freedom feeling, which is really interesting in a lot of ways. It was in some ways clashing a bit with the covid restrictions. I was a bit surprised about a lot of peoples resistance to the restrictions.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get or rent a bike!
Bring a good rain jacket and umbrella.
Try some dutch traditional food like Stroopwafles and some dutch traditions.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met some really nice people and learnt a lot academically.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There was most female exchange students in Amsterdam and as a physics student, it was weird being in such a shifted gender distribution.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
